notes.23576.2.2: Three tablets run together: 23576 (against Firmina), 27805 (a judicial curse on named opponents, addressed to Savus, god of the river Sava) and 35454 (to Dis Pater, Veracura and Cerberus against Eudemus, apparently over a vessel he is to return). Spelling is non-standard throughout; the edition's (!) sic-marks and alternative readings (#) are not reproduced. Cuba(lenses) is an unidentified ethnic or place name. 27805.1.10 'sse' is literally 'themselves'; 'against us' may be meant. B()ona (27805.1.17) is an unresolved abbreviation; 'their goods' is a guess. Muta Tacita (written Tagita) is the goddess of silence. 35454.7–8 is in Greek; ΔΜΟΗΡΜΗ is left as a magical word. {or} is a repeated word the edition deletes. m[anibu]s may be 'the Manes' or 'with [your] hands'; [d]eum stands for deorum, 'of the gods'. In 35454.18, '(at him)' renders the edition's added (ad); 'have you angry' is the idiom 'find you hostile'. In the last line only the ending -ate of a lost word survives.

nodes.text: May [you] shut Firmina off from all
and L(ucius) Licinius Sura, a Span(iard),
Valens: so that they may not be able
may he turn them from their minds,
not to speak against; of those wick-
ed men may he make the mouth dumb.
and Lucius Larcius, son of L(ucius), Cuba(lenses).
of ours; may they fall dumb, so that
they do not speak against us.
Given to the one who crushes.

[Eudemus t]o the r[ealm of the under]-

may you k[ill] him with the worst death; to those be-
[low] may you l[ead] him; may you gather up the same man
to the M[ane]s, servants of the infernal
